title.en: The Twins in the Womb: Esau and Jacob
title.zh: 母腹中的雙生：以掃與雅各

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Rebecca, barren for twenty years, conceives after Isaac's prayer — and the children struggle within her. God's oracle settles the nation's future: 'two nations are in thy womb... and the elder shall serve the younger'. The red, hairy Esau and the smooth heel-grasping Jacob are born.
summary.zh: 利百加不育二十年，以撒祈禱後懷孕——二子在腹中相爭。神諭定兩國之運：「兩國在你腹內……大的要服事小的。」紅髮多毛的以掃與光滑抓腳跟的雅各出生。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the LORD said unto her: 'Two nations are in thy womb, and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.' And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb. And the first came forth ruddy, all over like a hairy mantle; and they called his name Esau. And after that came forth his brother, and his hand had hold on Esau's heel; and his name was called Jacob.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 25:23-26 (public domain), lightly condensed.

title.en: A Pot of Red Stew: Jacob Buys the Birthright
title.zh: 一鍋紅湯：雅購長子名分

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The quiet tent-dweller Jacob cooks stew while the hunter Esau comes in famished. Jacob prices the stew at the birthright; Esau swears it away, eats, and 'despised his birthright' — the transaction that will govern both brothers' fates.
summary.zh: 安靜住帳的雅各煮湯，打獵歸來的以掃飢極。雅各以湯索長子名分；以掃起誓賣之，喫了，竟「輕看他長子的名分」——此交易定兩兄弟之命運。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Esau said: 'Behold, I am at the point to die; and what profit shall the birthright do to me?' And Jacob said: 'Swear to me first'; and he swore unto him; and he sold his birthright unto Jacob. And Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way. Thus Esau despised his birthright.

title.en: Isaac Digs Wells and Names Peace at Beersheba

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: In another famine Isaac is told 'go not down into Egypt'; like his father he passes his wife off as his sister to Abimelech, is caught, and protected. Repeatedly expelled from wells he has dug, he withdraws peaceably until at Beersheba his oath and a shared feast bind the Philistine king; there the LORD appears and renews the oath of Abraham.
summary.zh: 又逢饑荒，神命以撒「不要下埃及去」；如父，他向亞比米勒稱妻為妹，被識破而受護。屢掘井屢被逐，一再退讓；至別是巴，與非利士王立誓共宴；耶和華顯現，重申亞伯拉罕之誓。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the herdmen of Gerar did strive with Isaac's herdmen, saying: 'The water is ours.' And he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him. And they digged another well, and strove for that also; and he called the name of it Sitnah. And he removed from thence, and digged another well; and for that they strove not.

Abimelech came with his captain to force a treaty: 'Let there be now an oath betwixt us'. Isaac made a feast, they sware and parted in peace; that same day his servants found water. He named the place Beersheba — 'well of the oath' — and there the LORD appeared by night, saying 'I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not', renewing the covenant blessing. Paraphrase of Genesis 26:26-25 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Stolen Blessing: Isaac, Jacob, and Esau
title.zh: 竊取祝福：以撒雅各以掃

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Blind old Isaac asks Esau for venison before giving him the deathbed blessing. Rebecca overheard and directs Jacob in goatskins and borrowed robes; Isaac's hands smell of 'the smell of a field which the LORD hath blessed', and he blesses Jacob by mistake. Esau arrives too late, weeps a great and exceeding bitter cry, and only a lesser blessing remains — so he hates Jacob and resolves to kill him.
summary.zh: 目盲老以撒命以掃獻野味後受臨終祝福。利百加竊聞，令雅各披山羊皮衣扮兄；以撒嗅其香，「如耶和華賜福之田」，遂誤祝雅各。以掃遲至，放聲大慟，僅得次等祝福；於是恨雅各，圖殺之。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said: 'The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.' And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau's hands; so he blessed him.

Jacob lied outright — 'I am Esau thy firstborn' — served the savoury meat, and received the blessing: heaven's dew, fatness of earth, nations bowing, cursers cursed. Esau returned, and 'when Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob... Esau his son cried with an exceeding great and bitter cry': 'Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?' Isaac gave him fatness of earth and the sword's life, adding the prophecy that the yoke would one day be broken from his neck. Esau consoled himself by planning Jacob's death; Rebecca sent her younger son away to her brother Laban's house. Paraphrase of Genesis 27:24-45 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Fleeing his brother, Jacob sleeps at 'the place' with a stone for pillow and dreams of a stairway set on earth with angels ascending and descending on it. Above it stands the LORD, renewing Abraham's promise; waking, Jacob says 'Surely the LORD is in this place, and I knew it not', names it Bethel, and vows a tenth of all he has.
summary.zh: 逃兄的雅各在「那地方」以石為枕而眠，夢見梯立於地，天使在梯上上去下來。耶和華立於其上，重申亞伯拉罕之應許；醒而曰「這地方我竟不知道」，名之伯特利，並許什一奉獻。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a standing-stone (matzevah) etiology for Bethel's sanctuary; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it. And, behold, the LORD stood beside him, and said: 'I am the LORD, the God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed.'

Jacob awoke in awe: 'How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God'. He set the stone as a pillar, poured oil on it, and vowed: if God kept him on the road and brought him home in peace, 'then shall the LORD be my God', this stone God's house, and a tenth of all his. The dream-strairway remains the image of traffic between heaven and earth in Jewish and Christian tradition alike. Paraphrase of Genesis 28:16-22 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Jacob Meets Rachel at the Well of Haran

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Jacob arrives at a well in the East where flocks wait for a stone too heavy for one man. He asks the shepherds for Laban's whereabouts; as he speaks, Rachel arrives with her father's sheep. Jacob rolls the stone away with one effort, waters the flock, and kisses her — weeping aloud at finding his kinswoman.
summary.zh: 雅各至東方井旁，羊群待石，一人不能移。雅各問牧者拉班所在；言語間拉結驅羊而至。雅各一舉移石，飲羊，與拉結親嘴——認得親族，放聲而哭。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jacob rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother. And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept. And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother (kinsman), and that he was Rebecca's son; and she ran and told her father.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 29:10-12 (public domain), lightly condensed.

title.en: The Deceiver Deceived: Seven Years for Rachel, Then Leah
title.zh: 欺人者受欺：七年得拉結，先得利亞

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Jacob serves seven years for Rachel, 'and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her'. At the wedding night Laban substitutes the veiled elder daughter Leah; in the morning Jacob cries 'Why hast thou beguiled me?' and must serve seven more years — the trickster of the birthright cheated exactly as he cheated.
summary.zh: 雅各為拉結服事七年，「因深愛拉結，就看這七年如同幾天」。婚夜拉班以蒙面之長女利亞代之；晨起雅各呼曰「你為什麼欺哄我？」須再服事七年——昔日欺父賣名者，今遭同等之欺。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.

Laban gathered the men of the place and made a feast; in the evening he gave Jacob Leah his daughter, and Jacob went in to her. In the morning, 'behold, it was Leah', and Jacob demanded an explanation; Laban answered that the elder must marry first. 'Fulfil her week, and we will give thee this also' — so Jacob completed the bridal week and took Rachel too, serving Laban seven years more. Paraphrase of Genesis 29:22-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Sons Are Born: Names from the Nursery of Rivalry
title.zh: 眾子出生：相爭搖籃中的命名

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: God 'opened' the unloved Leah's womb and closed Rachel's; a naming war in verse follows — Reuben ('the LORD hath looked upon my affliction'), Simeon ('He heard'), Levi ('this time will my husband be joined unto me'), Judah ('this time will I praise the LORD'). Rachel envies and gives Jacob her handmaid Bilhah for Dan and Naphtali; Leah answers with Zilpah for Gad and Asher.
summary.zh: 神使失寵的利亞生育，閉拉結之腹；遂展開命名之詩——流便（「耶和華看見我的苦情」）、西緬（「耶和華聽見」）、利未（「這回丈夫必與我聯合」）、猶大（「這回我要讚美耶和華」）。拉結妒而以辟拉予雅各生但拿弗他利；利亞以悉帕生迦得亞設。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The naming verses are the tribal etiologies of Israel's twelve sons.

passages.text: And Leah conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Reuben; for she said: 'Because the LORD hath looked upon my affliction; for now my husband will love me.' And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said: 'Because the LORD hath heard that I am hated, He hath therefore given me this son also'; and she called his name Simeon.

Third came Levi, 'now this time will my husband be joined unto me'; fourth, Judah — 'this time will I praise the LORD', the name of Israel's royal tribe. When Rachel saw she bore none, she gave Bilhah to Jacob as surrogate; Bilhah bore Dan ('God hath judged me') and Naphtali ('wrestlings of God'). Leah, no longer bearing, answered with Zilpah's Gad ('a troop cometh') and Asher ('happy am I'). Paraphrase of Genesis 29:34-30:13 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Mandrake Bargain and the Birth of Issachar and Zebulun
title.zh: 風茄交易與以薩迦西布倫出生

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Reuben finds mandrakes — the love-apples of folklore — in the wheat harvest; Rachel asks for them, and Leah's answer is barbed: 'Wouldst thou take my son's mandrakes...?' The sisters trade: Rachel sells a night with Jacob for the fruit, and Leah bears a fifth and sixth son, Issachar and Zebulun, plus daughter Dinah. Rachel, at last, 'remembered' God and bore Joseph.
summary.zh: 流便割麥時得風茄——民間傳說之情果；拉結求之，利亞譏曰：「你為你兒子的風茄……？」姊妹交易：拉結以一夜易果；利亞生第五第六子——以薩迦、西布倫，並女底拿。拉結終蒙「眷顧」，生約瑟。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Motif 'folk-magic' interpretive for the mandrake love-charm lore (cf. Song 7:13).

passages.text: And Rachel said to Leah: 'Give me, I pray thee, of thy son's mandrakes.' And she said unto her: 'Is it a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and wouldest thou take away my son's mandrakes also?' And Rachel said: 'Therefore he shall lie with thee tonight for thy son's mandrakes.'

Jacob, told of the bargain, lay with Leah, who bore Issachar ('a reward', 'hire') and Zebulun ('dwelling') and afterwards Dinah. Then 'God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb', and she bore Joseph, saying 'The LORD shall add to me another son'. Paraphrase of Genesis 30:16-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Speckled Flocks: Jacob Outwits Laban

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Jacob asks only the speckled, spotted, and dark cattle as his wage; Laban agrees — then removes them all. Jacob answers with peeled wands before the watering troughs (folk selective breeding) and by breeding the strongest animals, 'and the man increased exceedingly' — until Laban's sons grow angry and Laban's face turns against him.
summary.zh: 雅各只求有斑有紋的牲畜為工價；拉班應允——隨即盡除去。雅各以削皮枝置水槽前（民間擇配法），又擇強壯者配種，「就極其發大」——直至拉班眾子怒而拉班色變。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jacob took him rods of fresh poplar, and of the almond and of the plane-tree; and peeled white streaks in them, laying the white which was in the rods before the flocks in the gutters at the watering troughs where the flocks came to drink. And the flocks conceived before the rods; and the flocks brought forth straked, speckled, and spotted.

Laban changed Jacob's wages ten times, but the angel of God later told Jacob in a dream that He had seen Laban's dealings. Jacob bred only the strong among the speckled, putting his own flocks apart, 'so the feebler were Laban's, and the stronger Jacob's'; the man grew very rich in flocks, men-servants, maids, camels, and asses. Paraphrase of Genesis 30:41-43 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Flight from Laban and the Pillar at Mizpah
title.zh: 逃離拉班與米斯巴之柱

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Told in a dream to 'return unto the land of thy fathers', Jacob slips away with his family while Laban is shearing sheep; Rachel steals her father's household teraphim and hides them in the camel's saddle. Laban pursues, searches the tents, and misses the idols in his daughter's saddle — then the two make a watch-peace at Mizpah: 'The LORD watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.'
summary.zh: 雅各夢中得諭「回你父親之地」，趁拉班剪羊毛攜家而逃；拉結竊父家神像藏於駝鞍。拉班追至，搜帳不得——偶像正藏其女鞍中。二人在米斯巴立守望之約：「願耶和華在你我中間鑒察。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Laban said to Jacob: 'What hast thou done, that thou hast stolen away unawares to me, and carried away my daughters as captives of the sword? ... Wherefore didst thou flee secretly, and steal away from me; and didst not tell me, that I might have sent thee away with mirth, and with songs, with tabret, and with harp?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 31:26-27 (public domain), ellipsis marks omitted clause.

passages.text: Laban searched Rachel's tent and found nothing — she sat on the camel's saddle and pleaded the custom of women. Enraged, Jacob recited twenty years of service, losses, and Laban's wage-cheating; Laban proposed a covenant. They raised a heap of stones and a pillar at Galeed/Mizpah, swore by the God of Abraham and the god of Nahor, and parted with a feast — Jacob returning toward Canaan with a family of eleven sons. Paraphrase of Genesis 31:34-54 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Left alone at night at the ford of Jabbok, Jacob wrestles a 'man' until the rising of the sun; the stranger touches the hollow of his thigh and demands release, but Jacob answers: 'I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.' He receives the name Israel — 'thou hast striven with God and with men, and hast prevailed' — and limps for the rest of his life.
summary.zh: 夜半獨處雅博渡口，雅各與一「人」摔跤直到日出；那人摸其大腿窩，求離去，雅各答：「你不給我祝福，我就不容你去。」遂得新名以色列——「你與神與人較力，都得了勝」——終身跛行。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Also explains the Israelite food custom of not eating the thigh sinew.

passages.text: And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was strained, as he wrestled with him. And he said: 'Let me go, for the day breaketh.' And he said: 'I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.'

'What is thy name?' — 'Jacob.' — 'Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel; for thou hast striven with God and with men, and hast prevailed.' Jacob named the place Peniel, 'the face of God', for he had seen God face to face and lived; the sun rose on him as he passed over, limping upon his thigh. 'Therefore the children of Israel eat not the sinew of the thigh which is upon the hollow of the thigh, unto this day.' Paraphrase of Genesis 32:27-33 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

region.en: Road to Shechem, land of Canaan

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Dreading his brother's four hundred men, Jacob bows seven times to the earth as Esau approaches — and Esau runs to meet him, embraces him, falls on his neck, and kisses him; and they weep. The stolen blessing ends not in blood but in weeping reconciliation, refusal of gifts turned gracious, and a parting: 'let me leave... with thee some of the folk that are with me' accepted at last.
summary.zh: 雅各懼兄四百人，分七隊俯伏；以掃奔而迎之，抱其頸與之親嘴，二人哭泣。竊來的祝福不終於血而終於泣中復和；推辭的禮物終被收下，兄弟分道：「願在你我中間有一些跟從我的人。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him; and they wept.

Esau asked about the children and the droves; Jacob said he had come to find grace in his lord's eyes, and pressed gifts on him — 'take, I pray thee, my blessing that is brought to thee; because God hath dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough'. They parted, Esau to Seir, Jacob to Succoth and then Shechem, where he bought ground and built an altar he called El-elohe-Israel — 'God, the God of Israel'. Paraphrase of Genesis 33:5-20 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Dinah and the Sons of Jacob at Shechem
title.zh: 底拿與雅各眾子在示劍

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Prince Shechem violates Jacob's daughter Dinah, then loves her. Jacob's sons answer treacherously: circumcision of every male in the city as bride-price; on the third day, while the men are sore, Simeon and Levi slaughter the city and the brothers plunder it. Jacob protests only the practical consequence — 'ye have brought trouble on me' — and the chapter ends in ominous silence.
summary.zh: 示劍王子玷辱雅各之女底拿，後而愛之。雅各眾子以詭計應之：全城男丁受割禮為聘禮；第三日，眾疼痛之際，西緬利未盡誅其城，兄弟擄掠。雅各只怪後果——「你們連累了我」——章末黯然無語。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The narrative presents the deception and massacre through the text's own morally ambiguous voice.

passages.text: And Jacob's sons came in from the field when they heard it; and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob's daughter; for such thing ought not to be done.

The sons answered Shechem's plea 'with guile': 'We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised' — let every male be circumcised, 'and will not their cattle and their substance and all their beasts be ours?' On the third day Simeon and Levi, Dinah's full brothers, took each man his sword and slew all the males; the rest plundered the city. Jacob said to Simeon and Levi: 'Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land.' Paraphrase of Genesis 34:13-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: God at Bethel Again: Burying the Foreign Gods
title.zh: 神再於伯特利：埋葬外邦神像

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel and dwell there. Jacob orders the household: 'Put away the strange gods that are among you' — and they hand over the teraphim and earrings, which he buries under the terebinth at Shechem. At Bethel God appears again, blesses him, and confirms: 'thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name.'
summary.zh: 神命雅各上伯特利居住。雅各命全家：「除掉你們中間的外邦神」——眾人交出神像與耳環，雅各埋於示劍橡樹下。神在伯特利再次顯現祝福，堅立其名：「你的名原是雅各，從今以後不要再叫雅各，要叫以色列。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they gave unto Jacob all the strange gods which were in their hand, and the rings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the terebinth which was by Shechem. And they journeyed; and a terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.

Jacob built an altar at Bethel — El-beth-el, 'God of Bethel', where God had revealed Himself in flight. Deborah, Rebecca's nurse, died and was buried under the oak below Bethel, called Allon-bacuth, 'oak of weeping'. God appeared again upon his return from Paddan-aram, blessed him, and re-named him Israel, repeating the older promises of nation and land. Paraphrase of Genesis 35:6-15 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Rachel Dies in Childbirth: Benjamin the Son of Sorrow
title.zh: 拉結產難而逝：便俄尼便雅憫

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 10th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Rachel travails hard on the road to Ephrath; the midwife tells her 'this is also a son'. Dying, she names him Ben-oni, 'son of my sorrow'; Jacob renames him Benjamin, 'son of the right hand'. Jacob sets a pillar on her grave 'which is there unto this day', and Rachel's tomb by Bethlehem becomes a shrine of memory — and of biblical prophecy's weeping mother.
summary.zh: 拉結於往以法他路上產難；收生婆曰：「又得一子。」臨終名子便俄尼，「憂患之子」；雅各改名便雅憫，「右手之子」。雅各立柱於其墳，「直到今日」——伯利恆旁拉結之墓遂成記憶之所，亦是聖經預言中哭泣之母。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Rachel's tomb remains a contested pilgrimage site; record describes text only.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when she was in hard labour, that the mid-wife said unto her: 'Fear not; for now thou shalt have another son.' And it came to pass, as her soul was in departing — for she died — that she called his name Ben-oni; but his father called him Benjamin. And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath — the same is Bethlehem.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Genesis 35:17-19 (public domain), lightly condensed.
